chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever acts without knowledge, what he corrupts will be more than what he corrects.

key_terms.عِلْم: 'ilm — knowledge; in Islamic jurisprudence, this includes both theoretical religious knowledge (fiqh) and practical wisdom; the hadith implies one must possess adequate knowledge before undertaking any action
key_terms.يُصْلِحُ: yuslihu — reforms, corrects, rectifies; the root s-l-h connotes moral uprightness and repair
key_terms.يُفْسِدُ: yufsidu — corrupts, spoils, causes disorder; the root f-s-d connotes moral and practical corruption

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about acting without knowledge in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warning against acting without proper knowledge. The hadith establishes a fundamental principle in Islamic epistemology: ignorant action leads to more harm than benefit, since one who lacks knowledge cannot foresee the consequences of their deeds. This teaching would have resonated with early Muslim scholars as a call to prioritize learning before religious practice, legal rulings, or social intervention.
